key_insight: Tensor-based fusion of multi-modal genomic and clinical data can reveal latent features that improve cancer risk stratification over unimodal approaches.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help support more accurate patient risk grouping using routinely relevant markers such as tumor purity, stage, and survival outcomes.
method: Unsupervised framework combining feature extraction, tensor decomposition, and clustering
Fused heterogeneous genomic and clinical datasets into latent representations
Compared multiple feature-extraction and clustering combinations
evidence_signal: Validated on LinkedOmics with 11,158 patients across 32 cancer types, using internal/external clustering metrics and clinical benchmarks; tSVD+GMM performed best.
watch_item: Results are based on retrospective multi-modal datasets and clustering benchmarks, so clinical deployment would need careful external validation and workflow integration.
paper_title: Tensor-based Fusion of Multi-modal Data for Predicting Cancer Risk Levels
